chief_complaint: increasing shortness of breath climbing stairs, dry cough, and fingers turning white/purple in cold for 3 years
hpi_details: 3-year history of progressive shortness of breath when walking uphill and climbing stairs, which has now worsened to dyspnoea after walking 100 metres on flat ground. Accompanied by a persistent dry cough and profound fatigue. For the past 5 years, has suffered from severe Raynaud's phenomenon where his fingers turn stark white, then purple and painful whenever exposed to cold temperatures or getting food from the refrigerator. Noticeably, his fingers have become swollen, tight, and thickened (sclerodactyly), making it difficult to make a full fist or remove his wedding ring. Also reports chronic severe heartburn and difficulty swallowing solid bread (dysphagia). Denies smoking.
ideas: thinks his systemic circulation disorder is causing scar tissue to build up inside his lungs and esophagus
concerns: terrified his lungs and skin will harden completely leading to suffocation
expectations: wants specific autoimmune blood tests, lung CT imaging, and immune-suppressing medication to halt the hardening
pmh: Raynaud's phenomenon x5 years, severe gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
medications: omeprazole 40mg OD, amlodipine 5mg OD for Raynaud's
social_hx: never smoked, zero alcohol, retired accountant, lives with wife

clinical_knowledge.topic: Systemic Sclerosis-associated Interstitial Lung Disease (SSc-ILD with NSIP pattern on HRCT and positive anti-Scl-70 antibodies) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Systemic Sclerosis-associated Interstitial Lung Disease (SSc-ILD with NSIP pattern on HRCT and positive anti-Scl-70 antibodies) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Multidisciplinary management between rheumatology and pulmonology, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: increasing shortness of breath climbing stairs, dry cough, and fingers turning white/purple in cold for 3 years

Key HPI features: 3-year history of progressive shortness of breath when walking uphill and climbing stairs, which has now worsened to dyspnoea after walking 100 metres on flat ground. Accompanied by a persistent dry cough and profound fatigue. For the past 5 years, has suffered from severe Raynaud's phenomenon where his fingers turn stark white, then purple and painful whenever exposed to cold temperatures or getting food from the refrigerator. Noticeably, his fingers have become swollen, tight, and thickened (sclerodactyly), making it difficult to make a full fist or remove his wedding ring. Also reports chronic severe heartburn and difficulty swallowing solid bread (dysphagia). Denies smoking.

Objective/Exam findings: Perform targeted rheumatological and pulmonary examination. Skin/Hands: inspect skin over fingers and hands -> demonstrates sclerodactyly (tight, shiny, thickened skin distal to metacarpophalangeal joints), digital pitting scars / ulceration, and periungual capillary fold dilatation/dropout on nailfold capillaroscopy. Face: microstomia (tight pursed lips) and telangiectasias. Chest auscultation: bilateral fine end-inspiratory Velcro crackles heard at the lung bases posteriorly. Autoimmune Serology: positive Antinuclear Antibody (ANA high titre), positive Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I antibody -> highly specific for Diffuse Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis and strongly predictive of progressive interstitial lung disease). PFTs / Spirometry: Restrictive pattern (reduced FVC, preserved FEV1/FVC ratio) accompanied by disproportionately severe reduction in DLCO ( predominant bilateral, symmetrical ground-glass opacities combined with fine reticulation and traction bronchiectasis in the lower lobes, with subpleural sparing and absence of coarse honeycombing). Check echocardiogram to screen for concurrent Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
Relevant background/PMH: Raynaud's phenomenon x5 years, severe gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
Current medications: omeprazole 40mg OD, amlodipine 5mg OD for Raynaud's
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Systemic Sclerosis-associated Interstitial Lung Disease (SSc-ILD with NSIP pattern on HRCT and positive anti-Scl-70 antibodies).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Community-acquired pneumonia without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe hypoxemia (SpO2 < 90%).
management_principles: Multidisciplinary management between rheumatology and pulmonology

After rheumatology/pulmonology confirm clinically significant or progressive SSc-ILD and complete baseline safety assessment, consider clinician-directed mycophenolate mofetil as preferred first-line immunosuppression; select dose, monitoring, and alternatives according to organ function, comorbidities, and local guidance.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 61M with 5-year Raynaud's and GORD presents with 3-year progressive exertional dyspnoea, dry cough, sclerodactyly, and skin thickening.
reference_soap.objective: Perform targeted rheumatological and pulmonary examination. Skin/Hands: inspect skin over fingers and hands -> demonstrates sclerodactyly (tight, shiny, thickened skin distal to metacarpophalangeal joints), digital pitting scars / ulceration, and periungual capillary fold dilatation/dropout on nailfold capillaroscopy. Face: microstomia (tight pursed lips) and telangiectasias. Chest auscultation: bilateral fine end-inspiratory Velcro crackles heard at the lung bases posteriorly. Autoimmune Serology: positive Antinuclear Antibody (ANA high titre), positive Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I antibody -> highly specific for Diffuse Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis and strongly predictive of progressive interstitial lung disease). PFTs / Spirometry: Restrictive pattern (reduced FVC, preserved FEV1/FVC ratio) accompanied by disproportionately severe reduction in DLCO (<50% predicted). High-Resolution CT (HRCT) Chest: confirms Non-Specific Interstitial Pneumonia (NSIP pattern -> predominant bilateral, symmetrical ground-glass opacities combined with fine reticulation and traction bronchiectasis in the lower lobes, with subpleural sparing and absence of coarse honeycombing). Check echocardiogram to screen for concurrent Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
reference_soap.assessment: Suspected Systemic Sclerosis-associated Interstitial Lung Disease; confirm extent/pattern with HRCT, PFTs/DLCO, autoimmune testing, and assessment for pulmonary hypertension. DDx: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (shows UIP honeycombing on HRCT and negative anti-Scl-70), Rheumatoid Arthritis-ILD, Idiopathic NSIP, Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.
reference_soap.plan: Urgently assess oxygenation and seek emergency care for severe breathlessness at rest, SpO2 below 90%, cyanosis, chest pain, syncope, confusion, or hemoptysis. Arrange multidisciplinary rheumatology and pulmonology evaluation. After confirmation of clinically significant or progressive SSc-ILD and baseline safety assessment, a specialist may prescribe and monitor mycophenolate; consider nintedanib only for documented progressive fibrotic ILD. Optimise reflux treatment and lifestyle measures with the treating clinician, and individualise PFT/DLCO and echocardiographic follow-up to disease severity and local pathways.

learning_objectives: Correlate Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, and anti-Scl-70 antibodies with Systemic Sclerosis-associated Interstitial Lung Disease
Interpret HRCT showing lower-lobe ground-glass opacities with subpleural sparing confirming Non-Specific Interstitial Pneumonia (NSIP)
Select mycophenolate mofetil over cyclophosphamide as preferred first-line disease-modifying immunotherapy in SSc-ILD
Integrate aggressive gastro-oesophageal reflux mitigation with anti-fibrotic co-prescribing to preserve forced vital capacity

teaching.one_liner: Pulmonology case presenting with increasing shortness of breath climbing stairs, dry cough, and fingers turning white/purple in cold for 3 years.
red_flags: Severe breathlessness at rest, cyanosis, or SpO2 below 90%
Chest pain, syncope, new confusion, or rapidly worsening exercise tolerance

must_ask.say: How has your breathlessness changed over the past three years, and do you have a dry cough with it?
Do your fingers turn white and then purple in the cold, and have you noticed your skin becoming tight or thick?
Do you have bad heartburn or trouble swallowing solid food like bread?

must_ask.objective: Family history and autoimmune serology screen
must_ask.say: Has anyone in your family had scleroderma, lupus, or another autoimmune condition?

must_ask.objective: Screen for pulmonary arterial hypertension symptoms
must_ask.say: Do you get lightheaded, have chest pressure, or notice your ankles swelling with the breathlessness?
